name: @oriui/headless — every core export, bundled (gzip)
message: What an app ships that imports the whole engine, measured through its chunks: the entry file alone is a re-export of a few hundred bytes.

name: @oriui/headless/vue — every composable, bundled, vue excluded (gzip)
message: The whole Vue adapter with the engine it bundles. It is the denominator for the useDialog entry below.

name: tree-shaking — useDialog alone from @oriui/headless/vue (gzip)
message: One composable must not pull the adapter: a jump toward the entry above means the barrel stopped tree-shaking, e.g. a module-scope side effect against "sideEffects": false.

name: tree-shaking ceiling — every @oriui/vue export bundled into one app (gzip)
message: This is the denominator the per-component entries below are judged against: what a consumer ships who imports the whole catalog. Raising it to make CI pass also raises the bar every tree-shaking entry is read against, so re-measure those too.

name: tree-shaking — OriKbd alone: a leaf stays ~1.5% of the ceiling, it must not drag in the other 33 (gzip)
message: OriKbd imports no sibling component, so this is the floor: importing one name out of the barrel must not pull the catalog. A jump toward the ceiling entry means the barrel stopped tree-shaking — look for a new cross-component import, or a module-scope side effect that contradicts "sideEffects": false in packages/vue/package.json.

name: tree-shaking — OriButton alone: pulls only the 2 siblings it renders (Icon, Spinner) (gzip)
message: OriButton legitimately pulls OriIcon and OriSpinner (it renders an icon slot and a loading spinner) and nothing else. A jump means a third sibling crept into its import graph — a cost every consumer of OriButton now pays.

name: tree-shaking — OriColorPicker alone: the heaviest component, 5 siblings, still a fraction of the ceiling (gzip)
message: OriColorPicker composes OriInput, OriSlider, OriButton, OriIcon and OriSpinner — the upper bound for a single component import. If it approaches the ceiling, composition has stopped being selective.
